figure1.title: The plunging price of thought
figure1.unit: USD per benchmark task at or above a fixed chance-adjusted accuracy threshold
transformations: Rename source columns: level -> threshold_adjusted_accuracy, model_label -> model, cost -> cost_usd_per_task, acc -> run_adjusted_accuracy.
Remove plotting-only columns label_drawn and trace_label. Preserve all 40 published record-setting data points.
caveats: Threshold and run scores are adjusted above guessing probability: adjusted=(raw-floor)/(1-floor). GPQA floor is 0.25, AIME floor is 0.001, FrontierMath and chess floors are 0. A 75% adjusted GPQA threshold means 81.25% raw accuracy.
Dates are model/price-version dates in upstream data, not the dates the authors ran evaluations.
These are sampled record costs, not average customer prices or production costs. Connecting them as a staircase assumes previous records remain available until the next observed record.
Benchmark performance is not synonymous with economic usefulness; coverage, benchmark overfitting and budget-truncation methodology limit interpretation.
The per-task metric includes reasoning-token usage and differs from older USD/million-token series.
Upstream repository has no standalone LICENSE file; the publisher explicitly licenses this published work CC BY 4.0. Source data attribution is retained.

figure2.title: Electricity consumption by data centres, 2020-2035
figure2.unit: TWh per year, all global data centres
transformations: Extract the chart data-chart-csv HTML attribute verbatim to raw CSV; no values digitized or interpolated.
Historical values retained for 2020-2025. Forecast base case retained for 2026-2035.
For projections, case_low_twh=Blank; case_high_twh=Blank+Case range. These follow the original stacked chart configuration.
caveats: Historical means IEA historical estimate, not a complete metered census.
The forecast band is the source's scenario range, not a statistical confidence interval.
All data-centre electricity is broader than AI-only consumption.
Use exact chart values: 485.1 TWh (2025) and 945.0 TWh (2030). The executive summary rounds them to 485 and 950 TWh.
Current draft presents source-supplied annual projections; future values are not observations.
The public chart has CSV download disabled but embeds the full licensed dataset in its HTML.

The independently rounded source components put the summed upper band 0.1 TWh below the base case in 2026-2028. Values are preserved; allow 0.1 TWh rounding tolerance rather than silently changing the data.
